summary.text: The Black–Scholes model is a mathematical model of a financial market containing derivatives, and its formula gives a theoretical estimate of the price of European-style options.
Its main principle is to hedge the option by buying and selling the underlying asset in a specific way so that risk is eliminated.
It assumes the stock price follows a geometric Brownian motion with constant drift and volatility, in a market with no fees and no riskless-profit opportunities.

facts.label: Nobel Prize
facts.value: Merton and Scholes received the 1997 economics prize

facts.label: Unobservable input
facts.value: Average future volatility of the underlying asset

facts.label: Earlier idea
facts.value: Bachelier's 1900 thesis first applied Brownian motion to pricing

facts.label: Stock model
facts.value: Geometric Brownian motion with constant drift and volatility

items.prompt: A bank has sold an option and worries the stock will move against it. What does the model suggest it do?

options.label: Keep the stock position fixed and hope
Buy and sell the underlying asset in a way that removes the risk
Sell the stock and never trade again
Wait until the option expires before doing anything

items.explain: The model's main principle is to hedge the option by buying and selling the underlying asset in a specific way to eliminate risk.

items.prompt: A trader plugs numbers into the formula. Which input cannot be looked up directly in the market?

options.label: The average future volatility of the asset
The strike price of the option
The current price of the stock
The time left until the option ends

items.explain: The formula has only one parameter that cannot be directly observed: the average future volatility, though it can be found from the prices of other options.

items.prompt: A broker charges a fee on every trade. Which assumption of the original model does this break?

options.label: The stock follows a geometric Brownian motion
The riskless rate stays constant
The market has no fees or costs
Stocks can be sold short

items.explain: The model assumes a frictionless market with no fees or costs, and later extensions added transaction costs.

items.prompt: Two options are identical except one has a higher market price. What does the model say about the volatility behind the higher price?

options.label: It is lower, because dearer options are safer
It is the same, as volatility does not affect price
It cannot be compared, as price and volatility are unrelated
It is higher, since option value rises with volatility

items.explain: The option value, put or call, is increasing in volatility, so it can be inverted to read a volatility from a price.

items.prompt: A trader finds a way to lock in a profit that beats the riskless rate, with no risk at all. Which assumption of the model rules this out?

options.label: No arbitrage opportunity
Frictionless trading
Constant volatility
Fractional buying and selling

items.explain: The model assumes there is no way to make a riskless profit in excess of the risk-free rate.

items.prompt: Nobody knows what path a stock will take. How can the model still give a derivative's price today?

options.label: It assumes the stock will never move
It copies the price from the day before
It builds a hedged position whose value does not depend on the stock price
It averages the prices of every stock in the market

items.explain: Even though the future path is unknown, a hedged position of stock and option can be made whose value will not depend on the stock price, which pins down the price.
